rationale.complete: Round 1 plus round 1b (2026-10-04): a room-index bug (open room segments dropped) was fixed and #33, #38, #44 and #51 rebuilt, with a switch (H41_ROOMS=old) that reproduces round 1, a per-period audit of changed lookups, an old-to-new table, a deterministic bootstrap and a re-run of the #51 synthetic validation. 32 replication periods, 4 native tests, channel attribution with in-cone controls, guarded confirm script re-frozen (not run). Round 2 must pre-register the matched jump and time-stamp the unlogged channel.
rationale.faithfulness: The logged light cone organizes the data where it binds: within-room adoptions almost never precede read-out (<= 4%, median 0.6%), 75-100% of cross-room adoptions in fixed two-room periods fall outside the cone, and NE42's merge/split moves cross-group pickup 80-860x as predicted (all unchanged by the 1b fix). But the pre-registered gating test failed (10-12/32; post hoc matched 22-24/32), #51's bridging claim reversed once rooms were fixed (51% in the cone, not 97%), a third of fast adoptions look co-generated, cadence and velocity predictions failed, and nothing is confirmed on the holdout.
rationale.usefulness: A computable diagnostic: logged chat explains almost no cross-room spread, and shared artifacts cannot be blamed from logs; human cross-posts (23-28x) are the only strongly enriched leak. Fixed rooms are strong cages for chat (merging multiplies cross-group pickup ~100x); rooms that agents hop between leak about half the time. Spread runs at about one hop per 1.5-5 talk turns, independent of call cadence. No validated control knob.

one_line: Novel items obey a logged read-out light cone in rooms and across NE42; the gating jump passes only post hoc; cross-room leaks stay untraceable.
